input.quote: AbbVie shall cease any and all Exploitation of Licensed Compounds and Licensed Products and transfer to Harpoon, or destroy (at Harpoon's sole election), copies of all data and Information generated by AbbVie in connection with the Exploitation of Licensed Compounds or Licensed Products
input.rationale: Article 12's exit mechanics run almost entirely in Harpoon's favour: Sections 12.6.1(c) and 12.7.2–12.7.8 require us to transfer or destroy data, regulatory materials and know-how on reversion, while nothing obliges Harpoon to provide any post-termination transition assistance or to return our data on a defined timeline. Section 9.7 (p0517/p0518) is the only data-return mechanic; it is mutual and includes destruction confirmation and a retention carve-out, but it is request-based, runs only "as soon as reasonably practicable" with no 30-day export deadline and no machine-readable format, and its retention carve-out does not extend to the separate destruction election in Section 12.6.1(c). That election lets Harpoon require immediate destruction of data we generated, with no carve-out for records we must keep under Applicable Law (including our own retention duty in Section 3.8.5), pharmacovigilance or litigation holds — the walk-away scenario of "immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination." The sell-off period in Section 12.10.2 gives some commercial wind-down but no data or transition support. We therefore propose the minimal preferred-position edits: a 30-day machine-readable transfer with a legal/archival retention carve-out in 12.6.1(c), and a new Section 12.6.6 giving us up to six months of transition assistance at our cost plus return and certified deletion of our data. Ninety days of assistance with a 30-day export would be an acceptable fallback.

proposal.summary: Add Harpoon-side wind-down/transition assistance and machine-readable data return on termination, and carve legally required records out of the destruction election in Section 12.6.1(c).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a reciprocal wind-down provision so that on termination Harpoon returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days and provides up to six (6) months of transition assistance at our cost, and we carved records we are required to keep under Applicable Law out of Harpoon's destruction election in Section 12.6.1(c). Our playbook requires an orderly data return and transition period before any deletion; we can live with 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

ops.oldText: transfer to Harpoon, or destroy (at Harpoon's sole election), copies of all data and Information generated by AbbVie in connection with the Exploitation of Licensed Compounds or Licensed Products
ops.newText: within thirty (30) days transfer to Harpoon, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, or destroy (at Harpoon's sole election), copies of all data and Information generated by AbbVie in connection with the Exploitation of Licensed Compounds or Licensed Products; provided that AbbVie may retain one (1) copy of, and shall not be required to destroy, any such data or Information to the extent reasonably necessary to comply with Applicable Law (including Section 3.8.5) or its pharmacovigilance obligations, or for litigation or archival purposes

ops.text: 12.6.6 Wind-Down Support. Upon any termination of this Agreement (in its entirety or with respect to any country or other jurisdiction), Harpoon shall, at AbbVie's request, (a) provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the effective date of such termination, at AbbVie's cost, to enable the orderly wind-down or transfer of AbbVie's activities hereunder (including with respect to Regulatory Documentation, safety data and ongoing clinical trials); (b) within thirty (30) days of such request, return to AbbVie, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all data and Information of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control; and (c) thereafter delete such data and Information from its systems (subject to Section 9.7) and certify such deletion in writing to AbbVie.
